headline_marked: Instagram's Adam Mosseri: [[Don't like AI?]] Don't have it in your feed
headline: Instagram's Adam Mosseri: Don't like AI? Don't have it in your feed
summary: Mosseri doesn't want to filter out AI content, but wants users to know if it's AI-generated
details: Instagram head Adam Mosseri doesn't want to filter out AI content on the platform, but argues users who don't like it 'shouldn't have it in your feed'. Mosseri believes people who love AI content 'should be able to have a feed that's just AI town'.

Mosseri acknowledged that detecting AI content is 'hard', and that Instagram may 'lose the ability' to pick up on AI posts as models improve. He suggests labeling non-AI-generated 'camera-captured content' instead.

Instagram will label AI-generated content, but won't give users an option to filter it out of their feed. The platform continues to embrace AI technology, including the launch of Meta's AI image generator, Muse Spark.

headline_marked: Xreal's $299 [[a01+ AR glasses now available]] for gamers, movie fans
headline: Xreal's $299 a01+ AR glasses now available for gamers, movie fans
summary: Lightweight AR glasses with 120Hz Micro-OLED displays, HDR10, 1,600 nits brightness
details: The Xreal a01+ AR glasses are designed for mainstream audiences who want a 'pocket cinema' for games and movies. They weigh just 62 grams, achieved by omitting a built-in camera.
The glasses feature dual-layer 120Hz Micro-OLED displays with HDR10 support and 1,600 nits brightness. They also upscale SDR content and employ a spatial stabilization algorithm.
The a01+ offers a virtual display 'equivalent to 147 inches at 4 meters' with a 50-degree field of view. It also has three color profiles and four audio modes.
The glasses have interchangeable front frames for customization and 3D printable accessories. They're available now for $299.
